title: Business records request
use_when: Use for collecting the federal tax records of a small business, whether or not it has employees; the employee, inventory, asset, travel and corporation items are switched on by tags.
note: Items follow the IRS lists of business records and employment tax records to keep. The IRS says to keep employment tax records for at least four years after filing the 4th quarter for the year; state requirements are not covered.

irs-records.name: IRS, What kind of records should I keep (page last reviewed or updated 03-Aug-2026)

pub-583.name: IRS Publication 583, Starting a Business and Keeping Records (Rev. December 2024)

irs-emp-records.name: IRS, Employment tax recordkeeping (page last reviewed or updated 12-Jun-2026)

situations.inventory: Does the business buy items to resell, or materials to make products?
situations.assets: Does the business own property such as machinery or furniture that it uses in the business?
situations.travel: Does the business deduct travel, gift or transportation expenses?

items.label: Business books: accounting journals and ledgers, or the accounting software file
items.detail: The books must show gross income, deductions and credits.

items.label: Business checking account records: checkbook, copies of deposit slips and bank statements
items.detail: Publication 583 calls the business checkbook the main source for entries in the business books. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Copies of filed tax returns
Minutes of board of directors' meetings
Cash register tapes
Deposit information (cash and credit sales), including bank deposit slips
Receipt books
Sales invoices
Credit card charge slips
Forms 1099-MISC received
Forms 1099-NEC received
Canceled checks or other documents showing proof of payment or electronic funds transferred
items.detail: Documents should identify the payee, the amount paid, proof of payment, the date incurred, and a description of the item showing the amount was for purchases.

items.label: Cash register tape receipts
Credit card receipts and statements
Purchase invoices
Canceled checks or other documents showing proof of payment or electronic funds transferred
items.detail: Documents should identify the payee, the amount paid, proof of payment, the date incurred, and a description of the item purchased or service received.

items.label: Cash register tape receipts
Account statements
Credit card receipts and statements
Expense invoices
Petty cash slips for small cash payments
Records that prove travel, gift and transportation expenses
items.detail: The IRS page refers to Publication 463 for the elements that must be proved.

items.label: For each asset: when and how it was acquired, purchase price, cost of any improvements, and how it was used
items.detail: Also: Section 179 deduction taken, deductions taken for depreciation, and deductions taken for casualty losses.

items.label: For each asset sold or disposed of: when and how, selling price and expenses of sale
Purchase and sales invoices for assets
Real estate closing statements
Canceled checks or other documents that identify payee, amount and proof of payment
Employer identification number (EIN)
items.detail: Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Amounts and dates of all wage, annuity and pension payments
Amounts of tips reported by employees, and the record of all allocated tips
Fair market value of in-kind wages paid
Names, addresses, Social Security numbers and occupations of employees and recipients
items.detail: Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Any employee copies of Form W-2 and W-2c returned as undeliverable
Dates of employment for each employee
Periods for which employees and recipients were paid while absent due to sickness or injury
items.detail: Include the amount and weekly rate of payments the employer or third-party payers made to them.

items.label: Copies of income tax withholding certificates (Forms W-4, W-4P, W-4S and W-4V)
items.detail: Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Dates and amounts of tax deposits made, and acknowledgment numbers for deposits made by EFTPS
Copies of employment tax returns filed and confirmation numbers
Records of fringe benefits and expense reimbursements provided to employees, including substantiation
Documentation to substantiate any credits claimed
items.detail: The IRS page says records for qualified sick and family leave wages for leave taken after March 31, 2021, and for employee retention credit qualified wages paid after June 30, 2021, should be kept for at least 6 years.

items.label: Documentation of any employer or employee share of social security tax deferred and paid for 2020
